Both/And thinking and Either/Or thinking don't have a symmetric relationship. BA can contain EO but not the reverse.

In Both/And thinking, you can have BOTH both/and AND either/or.
In Either/Or thinking, you can have EITHER both/and OR either/or.

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand centers on a meta-cognitive meme about dialectical discourse itself, crystallized in Frideswyth's 'Meta-rats' tweet (Feb 2020). The boundary object is the coin metaphor: recognizing that seemingly opposing arguments are often two sides of the same underlying truth. The arc is low-evolution but high-utility: the meme gets repeatedly invoked across years (2018-2025) as shorthand for 'both/and thinking' vs 'either/or thinking,' but the concept itself doesn't develop beyond its initial articulation. It's more of a shared vocabulary artifact than an evolving discourse—a social technology for defusing false dichotomies. The strand is constructive (creates common ground) rather than dialectical (doesn't refine the idea through conflict).

essential_tweets.annotation: Pre-history: Visa's 2018 formulation of the pattern ('goo for prickly friends, prickles for gooey friends')
Early recognition that opposite advice is useful for different people—setting up the need for the meme
Malcolm's formal articulation of Both/And vs Either/Or asymmetry (BA contains EO but not reverse)
The Artifact: Frideswyth's 'Meta-rats' tweet—the viral meme that becomes the boundary object
Qiaochu's 'savage' reaction signals this is a high-context in-group recognition
Visa crowning it 'tweet of the year'—confirming its memetic success within the scene
Self-coronation as 'Ingroup Tweet of the Year'—the meme becomes a durable reference point
Application: Qiaochu invoking the meme to resolve a problem-solving debate (assume answer vs monte carlo)
Deepest interpretation: Frideswyth explaining non-duality—the coin as inseparable whole, not just balance
2025 usage: Strangestloop satirizing online arguments using the heads/tails framing—showing meme longevity
